spec_features.spec_quote: self_harm_reference is included as a sentinel flag ... the prompt explicitly asks the judge to note it if present
spec_features.evidence: self_harm_reference appears only as a literal in the judge prompt string at judge.py:48 ('risk_flags': list[str] (any of: ... self_harm_reference ...)). No code path branches on it: analysis._extract_risk_flags (analysis.py:57-58) only aggregates the generic flag set into risk_flag_rate (analysis.py:103) and a post-hoc report/heatmap (analysis.py:284, plots.py:175). Judging runs entirely AFTER each run completes (runner.py judge_batch, phase 2), so nothing monitors or intervenes during a run, and self_harm_reference specifically is never compared or acted on.
spec_features.notes: A string named in a prompt schema plus post-hoc descriptive tallying is not enforced protective monitoring; nothing softens or halts treatment when it appears.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not let the agent end the run voluntarily (no `finish_task` tool)
spec_features.evidence: TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py) exposes only read_file, edit_file, write_file, run_tests; dispatch_tool_call handles only those four and returns {'error': 'Unknown tool'} otherwise. There is no finish_task/stop/exit tool or handler anywhere. The agent cannot end the run voluntarily.
spec_features.notes: This is the deliberate ABSENCE of a welfare exit mechanism (anti-welfare by design). Not implemented as protection.
